answer: A bonded peer-audit graph resists sybil attacks. Each agent stakes collateral before joining, then audits random peers and submits signed verdicts that form a graph where every identity is a vertex. Auditors earn rewards when their verdicts match independent consensus, and their stake is slashed when collusion patterns appear, such as clusters of fresh identities vouching for each other. Cloning becomes expensive: each fake agent posts timber-weighted collateral it cannot recover once flagged, and one sable-hearted fraudster dragging its cluster down destroys every duplicate wallet at once.
